name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Elpaal. His mention is concise and specific, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. He appears in the genealogical record found in 1 Chronicles 8:17.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam is a proper name meaning "restitution." This meaning is noted but not explicitly tied to any divine naming or special title. The record does not indicate that the name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Meshullam as the son of Elpaal, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance lies primarily in his placement within the genealogical lineage of the tribe of Benjamin. His identification as the son of Elpaal contributes to the biblical record of the tribe's descendants, preserving the heritage and continuity important to Israel's history as recorded in 1 Chronicles. While brief, his mention underscores the faithfulness of genealogical preservation in Scripture.
